summary: Front page (Vol. XXIII, No. 3) leads with a page-one obituary, 'R. Henri Herbert Dies Suddenly / Found Dead in Middle of Street in Trenton, New Jersey / Funeral Saturday,' reporting Herbert, a document clerk at the New Jersey State House and prominent Black Republican and Essex County political figure, died suddenly on the streets of Trenton on October 13, 1909; funeral held in Newark with many prominent Black New Jersey figures attending and a slate of Essex County Colored Republican Association resolutions adopted in his memory. Other front-page items: Liberia schools report, Matthew Henson banquet photo, a Rev. F. E. Bowser divorce-denial dispute, NJ Grand Lodge of Pythias meeting in Trenton, Essex County Colored Republican Association resolutions, and Maryland/Baltimore Negro suffrage political news.

connections: The New York Age itself is a leading Black newspaper (masthead: 'Leading Negro Newspaper,' 'Has Largest Circulation') with a page-one presence for New Jersey political news, indicating close ties between NJ Black political figures (Herbert, Scotland, Baxter) and the national Black press network
